 :Judgment:

1. The petitioner filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1989, seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/ M.V.C.No.4248/2021 3 SCCH - 7 for the injures sustained by him in the road traffic accident occurred on 06.09.2021 2.

It is the case of the petitioner that, on 06.09.2021 at about 7.30 p.m., he was riding motorcycle bearing registration No.KA06EY7201 from Nidasale to Mallanakuppe side, reached near Nidasale Govt. Collage, SH33, Maddur Kunigal Road, Huliyurdurga Hobli, Kunigal Taluk,
Tumakuru, at that time one Tipper Lorry bearing registration No.KA53D2007, came in a rash and negligent manner and came on wrong lane, he lost control over his Tipper Lorry put the brake and petitioner vehicle dashed against the Tipper lorry and due to impact he fell down and sustained injuries to all over the body.

Immediately he was shifted to Maddur Govt. Hospital, after first aid treatment he was shifted to Mandya Govt. Hospital and then shifted to NIMHANS hospital Bangalore and again he was shifted to Mandya Govt. Hospital, wherein he M.V.C.No.4248/2021 4 SCCH - 7 took treatment as inpatient.
Prior to the accident he was hale and healthy and aged about 21 years and he was working as driver and earning Rs.20,000/ p.m.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident he became permanently disabled.

This accident is took place due to the negligence of the driver of the Tipper Lorry bearing registration No.KA53D2007 as such the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to him.
Hence, he prayed to allow the petition.
3. In response to the notice, the respondent No.1 and 2 are appeared through their counsel and they have filed their separate written statement.
4. In the written statement the respondent No.1 denied the entire contention of the petitioner.
Further contended that the claim of the petitioner is highly exorbitant, excessive and imaginary and Manjunatha.

5. The respondent No.2  insurer denied the entire contentions of the petitioner.

Further the respondent No.2 admitted that they have issued the Insurance Policy to the Good Carrier Truck bearing registration No.KA53D2007 and their liability is subjected to terms and conditions of the policy.

The respondent No.2 contended that as on the date of the accident the driver of the Goods Carrier Truck bearing registration No.KA53D2007 was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the same and not having valid permit as on the date of alleged accident,
hence it is violation of terms and conditions of the Insurance Policy.
Hence, on all these grounds, the respondent No.2 has prayed for dismissal of claim petition.
On the basis of above pleadings following Issues were framed.

:: I S S U E S ::
(1) Whether petitioner proves that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent act of driving of Tipper Lorry bearing registration No.KA53D2007 and as a result, he sustained injuries?
(2) Whether the Petitioner proves the age and earnings of the Petitioner as stated in the claim petition?
(3) Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?

(4) What order or award?

sentences.text: Issue No.1: The petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and in his examination in chief he deposed as per the M.V.C.No.4248/2021 8 SCCH - 7 contentions taken by him and got marked FIR as per Ex.P 1, Complaint as per Ex.P2, Spot mahazar as per Ex.P.3, Seizure mahazar as per Ex.P 4, IMV Report as per Ex.P.5, Wound Certificate as per Ex.P.6 and Charge Sheet as per Ex.P.7.
By perusing these documents it is clearly goes to show that this accident was took place due to the negligence on the part of driver of Tipper Lorry bearing registration No.KA53D2007.

Further in the crossexamination of PW.1, he deposed that he is working as TATA Ace driver and at the time of accident he was riding the motorcycle of his father at a speed of 10 - 15 km and he has seen the lorry within 100 meters and his vehicle is having light and in this accident his motorcycle front doom and mudguard are damaged.
He denied that by consuming the alcohol he was riding the motorcycle and dashed to the Lorry.

Further he deposed that after the accident he was admitted in the hospital and his parents are looking after him as such it is M.V.C.No.4248/2021 9 SCCH - 7 not possible for him to lodge the complaint immediately after the accident.
He denied that as himself has dashed to the lorry as such immediately they have not lodged the complaint.
He denied that only with an intention to get compensation by colluding with the police after three days of the accident they have lodged false complaint against the driver of the Lorry.
He denied that only to get compensation he is deposing falsely.
From the evidence of PW.1 it is clear that while he was riding his motorcycle at that time due to the negligence of the driver of the Lorry this accident was took place.
11. Further the respondent No.2 got examined their Senior Manager as RW.1 and in his examination in chief he deposed that as per contention taken by them.
Further he got marked Policy copy as per Ex.R.1.
In his cross examination he admitted that as on the date of the accident the policy issued to the Tipper Lorry bearing registration M.V.C.No.4248/2021 10 SCCH - 7 No.KA53D2007 was in force.
Further deposed that the police have filed Charge Sheet wrongly against the driver of the Tipper Lorry.
He denied that he is deposing falsely that this accident was took place due to the negligence of the rider of the motorcycle.
He denied that only with an intention to escape from the liability of paying compensation to the petitioner he is deposing falsely.
From the evidence of RW.1 nothing worth is brought on record to show that there is no negligence on the part of the driver of the Tipper Lorry bearing registration No.KA53D2007.

Hence from the oral evidence of PW.1 and RW.1 it is clear that this accident was occurred only due to the negligence of the driver of the Tipper Lorry bearing registration No.KA53D2007.
12.

It is the contention of the respondent No.2 that there is no negligence on the part of the driver of the lorry and there is delay of three days in lodging the complaint and petitioner M.V.C.No.4248/2021 11 SCCH - 7 colluding with the police lodged false complaint against the driver of the Tipper Lorry bearing registration No.KA53 D2007
as such they are not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner.

Further the petitioner has got reply issued by the owner of the Tipper lorry to the notice issued under Section 133 of MV Act wherein by perusing the same it goes to shows that on 06.09.2021 the Tipper Lorry bearing registration No.KA M.V.C.No.4248/2021 16 SCCH - 7 53D2007 was met with RTA.
Hence by perusing all these documents they clearly goes to shows that this accident was took place due to the negligence of the driver of the Tipper Lorry bearing registration No.KA53D2007.
Further by perusing the Wound Certificate marked as per Ex.P.6 it goes to shows that in this accident the petitioner has sustained injuries and for the injuries he has taken treatment.

15. The respondent No.2 contended that there is delay of three days in lodging the complaint and the petitioner by colluding with the police lodged false complaint against the driver of the Tipper Lorry bearing registration No.KA53D 2007, hence the case of the petitioner is not acceptable one.

By perusing the complaint it is clearly goes to shows that the complaint was lodged on 09.09.2021 at about 330 p.m., hence it is clear that after three days of the alleged accident the complaint was lodged.

The petitioner in his cross M.V.C.No.4248/2021 17 SCCH - 7 examination clearly deposed that as his parents were attending him in the hospital as such immediately after the accident they could not able to lodge the complaint.

By perusing the medical records marked as per Ex.P.10,
Discharge Summary marked as per Ex.P.11 they goes to shows that due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner was admitted in the hospital as such they could not able to lodge the complaint immediately after the accident.

Further mere delay in lodging the complaint is not a ground to reject the claim petition as per the authority reported in (2011) 4 SCC 693 in between Ravi V/s Bhadrinarayana wherein it is held that delay in lodging the FIR cannot be a ground to dismiss the case of the claimant, in this present case on hand there is delay of three days and petitioner has explained why delay was caused in lodging the complaint.
Hence the contention of the respondent No.2 is not acceptable one.

Hence by perusing M.V.C.No.4248/2021 18 SCCH - 7 the entire oral and documentary evidence I am of the considered view that this accident was took place due to the negligence of the driver of the Tipper Lorry bearing registration No.KA53D2007 and in this accident the petitioner has sustained injuries.
Hence, I answered the Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
16. Issue No.2:

The petitioner contended that as on the date of accident he was aged about 21 years and he was working as driver, and thereby earning Rs.20,000/ p.m. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident he became permanently disabled.

This accident was took place on 06.09.2021.
Hence, the age of petitioner is considered at 21 years as on the date of accident.

sentences.text: So for as income of the petitioner is concern the petitioner contended that he was working as driver and thereby earning Rs.20,000/ p.m.
In support of this contention the petitioner has not produced any documents to show that he was earning Rs.20,000/ p.m.

Hence in the absence of the acceptable material with regard to the income, by considering the occupation, age the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.15,000/ p.m., and the occupation of the petitioner is considered as driver.
Hence, I answered the Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
19. Issue No.3:

The petitioner contended that in the accident he has sustained deep lacerated wound over the left forehead, lacerated wound over the upper lip and lacerated wound over the back of neck and due to the said injury he is permanently disabled.
In this regard the petitioner has produced Wound Certificate as per Ex.P.6 and Discharge M.V.C.No.4248/2021 20 SCCH - 7 Summary marked as per Ex.P.11.

By perusing the same they goes to shows that due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has taken treatment at Mandya Institute of Medical Sciences and Teaching Hospital, Mandya as an inpatient from 07.09.2021 to 13.09.2021.

sentences.text: But the petitioner has not produced any acceptable evidence to show that due to the injuries sustained in the accident he has became permanently disabled.
Under such circumstances the question of granting compensation under the head of loss of future earnings does not arise at all.

20. No doubt in the accident the accident the petitioner has sustained deep lacerated wound over the left forehead, lacerated wound over the upper lip and lacerated wound over the back of neck it shows that due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has took treatment in Mandya Government as an inpatient for 7 days which shows that definitely the petitioner has suffered some pain M.V.C.No.4248/2021 21 SCCH - 7 due to the injuries sustained in the accident, hence an amount of Rs.50,000/ is awarded towards pain and sufferings.

21. Further due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner might have taken rest for at least for a period of one month, hence an amount of Rs.15,000/ is awarded under the head of loss of earning during the period of treatment and rest.

Further due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner was admitted as an inpatient and discharged from the hospital and during that period the petitioner might have taken an assistance of an attendant and might have taken nutritious food
hence an amount of Rs.10,000/ is awarded under the head of loss of attendant and nourishment charges.
22. Further the petitioner has produced the hospital and medicine bills marked as per Ex.P.13 for an amount of M.V.C.No.4248/2021 22 SCCH - 7 Rs.3,538/.
Hence an amount of Rs.3,538/ is awarded under the head of hospital and medicine charges.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation under the following heads;
Towards pain and sufferings Rs. 50,000.00 Towards loss of income Rs. 15,000.00 during period of treatment and rest Towards attendant and Rs. 10,000.00 nourishment charges Towards hospital and medical Rs. 3,538.00 expenses Total Rs. 78,538.00

Hence the petitioner is entitled for just and reasonable compensation amount of Rs.78,538/.
Manjunatha.

sentences.text: While answering the issue No.1 this Tribunal comes to the conclusion that, accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of Tipper Lorry bearing registration No.KA53 D2007.

The petitioner contended that the respondent No.1 is the owner and the respondent No.2 is the insurer of the said vehicle they are jointly and severally liable to pay M.V.C.No.4248/2021 23 SCCH - 7 compensation to him.
The respondent No.2 has admitted that as on the date of the accident the policy issued to the said Tipper Lorry bearing registration No.KA53D2007 was in force.
Nothing worth is brought on record to show that there is violation of terms and conditions of the policy by the owner of the Tipper Lorry bearing registration No.KA53D2007.

Hence the respondent No.1 being the owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurer of the Tipper Lorry bearing registration No.KA53D2007 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition.
Hence, I answered the issue No.3 in partly affirmative.

24. Issue No.4: For the above stated reasons I proceed to pass the following;
M.V.C.No.4248/2021 24 SCCH - 7 :ORDER:
Claim petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with costs of Rs.1,000/.
Petitioner is awarded just and reasonable compensation of Rs.78,538/ (Rupees Seventy Eight Thousand Five Hundred and Thirty Eight Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition to till the date of depositing of the compensation amount in the court.
The respondent No.2 being insurer of Tipper Lorry bearing registration No.KA 53 D2007 is directed to deposit the awarded compensation amount in the Court within 02 month from the date of this judgment.
Draw award accordingly.

:APPORTIONMENT:
On deposit of compensation amount entire compensation amount is to be M.V.C.No.4248/2021 25 SCCH - 7 released in favour of the petitioner under E payment and after verifying the stay order from the Hon'ble Appellate Court.

15. The respondent No.2 contended that there is delay of three days in lodging the complaint and the petitioner by colluding with the police lodged false complaint against the driver of the Tipper Lorry bearing registration No.KA53D 2007, hence the case of the petitioner is not acceptable one.

Discharge Summary marked as per Ex.P.11 they goes to shows that due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner was admitted in the hospital as such they could not able to lodge the complaint immediately after the accident.
Further mere delay in lodging the complaint is not a ground to reject the claim petition as per the authority reported in (2011) 4 SCC 693 in between Ravi V/s Bhadrinarayana wherein it is held that delay in lodging the FIR cannot be a ground to dismiss the case of the claimant, in this present case on hand there is delay of three days and petitioner has explained why delay was caused in lodging the complaint.
